title: Tech Note: 4D Ajax Framework JavaScript Injection
author: Josh Fletcher, Technical Support Engineer, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note documents a low-level technique for injecting and executing raw JavaScript returned from a 4D Developer Defined Window method, specific to the subscription-based 4D Ajax Framework (4DAF) that shipped as part of the short-lived 4D Web 2.0 Pack. The entire 4DAF/DDW/Daxipedia ecosystem it depends on has been discontinued, and manually parsing XML responses and calling eval() to inject script is a pattern modern web development actively avoids for security reasons. The underlying idea of a server pushing executable client behavior remains conceptually related to later techniques (e.g. server-driven UI, WebSockets, or Hotwire-style patterns), but as a practical guide it is entirely obsolete.
related_updates: 4D Ajax Framework and the 4D Web 2.0 Pack were discontinued and are no longer part of any current 4D product
4D's built-in Web Server and modern web component/Qodly tooling superseded the 4DAF approach for building web UIs
Injecting raw script via eval() on parsed XML responses is now considered an anti-pattern in modern web security practice
